comparison.objective: Candidate commissions a shock absorber for safe stopping; pr-71 calibrates around a faulty angle gauge and levels a hinged platform.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate manipulates a recessed setscrew and rotary collar under counterhold, then cycles a carriage. pr-71 relocates/orients a gauge, obtains reference and platform readings, and presses UP/DOWN controls for closed-loop leveling.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires two non-bottoming impact cycles and lock retention. pr-71 requires reference and platform readings with hands clear, true tilt within 0.15°, and controlled button use.
comparison.reason: Both include iterative adjustment from observed response, but their tested physical mechanisms differ substantially: retained rotary damper tuning under tool torque versus instrument-referenced platform leveling by buttons. The candidate still omits numeric rebound, overload, and drift thresholds.
